answer_1.quote: We propose an unsupervised, multi-stage framework. It first employs an LLM to decompose the user's intent to guide an iterative data extraction and refinement process from the document. Subsequently, it selects an appropriate chart type using predefined visualization heuristics before generating the final chart.
datasets: 1,242 <intent, document, chart> tuples from financial reports and scientific articles
answer_1.outputs: statistical charts in executable Matplotlib code and structured JSON format representing chart data

answer_2.quote: We propose CHARTEVAL, an attribution-based metric that uses structured textual representations for charts, and avoids reliance on visual decoding altogether.

answer_3.quote: Using a simpler LLM-based metric, on the other hand, where the generated chart tuples and reference table values are given to an LLM which is then instructed to provide a rating for data accuracy, we note a much lower r = 0.39.
methods: LLM-based metric for data accuracy rating

answer_4.quote: To qualitatively validate our approach, we conduct human surveys to compare the model-generated charts against references. Each evaluation instance consists of an intent, ground truth (GT) chart, its corresponding GT table, along with three AI-generated charts (from our approach and two baselines), which are anonymized and randomized to eliminate any biases. We hire three expert annotators...
answer_4.guideline: Each criterion is rated on a four-point scale: Minimal, Partial, Most, and Full, where Minimal indicates the chart does not meet expectations at all, and Full represents an ideal chart.
